observations: The candidate supports all four core traits at whole-view scale and meets the supplied catalogue finish floor.
The reference's cropped top and overlapping background vegetation limit exact silhouette comparison; specimen correspondence is unknown.

findings.observation: Long, finely leafed hanging strands, an irregular cascading crown, and visibly marked silvery-gray stems jointly support the reference character.

Upper branch fans are more exposed and visually wiry than the photograph's leafy shoulders. Softening their prominence would improve resemblance, but the whole crown retains its fine pendulous character.

The candidate's fine geometry, coherent silhouette, foliage detail, and trunk treatment meet the stylized whole-view finish demonstrated by the spruce anchor. No clear construction defect warrants blocking at this floor.

coverage.explanation: Numerous long, fine leafy shoots descend steeply around the candidate's crown, forming conspicuous curtains like those in the photograph.

Exposed candidate stems show silvery-gray surfaces with irregular dark streaks and patches. They are darker overall than the photographed white trunks, but the pale/dark marked character remains visible; fine bark texture is not assessed.
Small discrete leaf flecks trace slender hanging shoots, preserving the reference's fine stippled texture even where curtains overlap densely.

Unequal elevated tufts, broad outward shoulders, and long descending margins support the observed crown character. Exact top shape and full reference width are not required because those boundaries are clipped or obscured.
Both views show a comparatively upright stem and a conspicuous outward-leaning stem. This supports the visible divergence only; the photograph does not establish their exact basal connection.
Overlapping curtains produce dark interior regions interspersed with narrow openings and a finely broken perimeter in both images.
Visible candidate branches extend outward and bend into descending growth, matching the limited exposed arches in the photograph. Hidden junction topology remains unestablished.
Both images display pale green flecks, medium green foliage, and very dark recesses. This is a match of visible tonal range, without inferring intrinsic leaf color.
Candidate drapes vary visibly in length and density, with isolated outer strands and compact overlapping curtains, consistent with the reference's within-crown variation.
Unequal crown heights, lateral masses, and openings support asymmetry in both views. Their exact placement need not correspond between specimens of unknown relationship.
